summary: Self-improving agent loop: agent edits a training script, runs a time-boxed experiment, measures performance, keeps or discards the change, and repeats. Ran 700 experiments in 2 days on one GPU finding 20 optimizations.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — the core pattern (run→measure→keep/discard) maps to what AgentForge's orchestration loop does with Linear issues, but autoresearch targets ML training pipelines, not code-delivery pipelines. Also falls into the RL training loop red-flag category and the backlog was full this run.

source: DARWIN: Dynamic Agentically Rewriting Self-Improving Network
summary: Genetic-algorithm-style orchestration of GPT agents that mutate each other's training code; best-performing agents selected each iteration. Evolutionary multi-agent system for ML training code improvement.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — requires RL/evolutionary infrastructure and is targeted at training-code mutation, not issue-to-PR delivery pipelines. Explicit red-flag category (RL training loops).

summary: Self-improving system that iteratively modifies its own code and validates each change with coding benchmarks. Published at ICLR 2026. Achieves open-ended self-evolution.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — speculative meta-level self-rewriting; AgentForge's design deliberately avoids prompt self-evolution. Red-flag category.

source: DarwinX: Evolving Agent Harnesses Through Natural Selection
summary: Treats agentic self-evolution as selection over a population of harnesses with the model frozen; maintains an archive of alternative lineages for recombination. August 2026.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — population-based harness evolution is speculative and premature; AgentForge's sequential deterministic state machine is a deliberate design choice.

source: Agent Memory Frameworks 2026 Survey (Mem0, Letta, Graphiti, Dakera)

source: AI Agent Retry and Failure Classification Patterns 2026
summary: Production patterns for classifying agent failures (transient, rate-limit, validation, model, infrastructure) and applying appropriate retry strategies (exponential backoff, circuit breaker, fallback, escalation).
relevanceToAgentForge: High — maps directly to AgentForge's subprocess failure handling gap, but this theme is already tracked by open issue HID-167 (automatic retry with failure classification).

source: LangGraph 1.0 GA — per-node timeouts and DeltaChannel (Q2 2026)

relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge uses CLI subprocesses (ProcessRunner), not LangGraph graph nodes. Per-node timeout concepts are interesting but don't translate to AgentForge's architecture directly.

relevanceToAgentForge: Low — different tech stack (Python/.NET), API-client model vs AgentForge's CLI subprocess model. No applicable patterns.
